notable_absence.finding: Step 3 ('Choose a Storage Backend') is presented in this page's numbered create-flow without any stated bucket-type gate, and its own screenshots show the Storage Backend selector alongside a Couchbase-type bucket. Only the sibling page, edit-bucket.md, states 'This setting is only available for Couchbase buckets on Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition.' A reader of create-bucket.md alone could believe Storage Backend is offered for Ephemeral buckets too (which would be a category error, since Ephemeral buckets have no disk persistence at all) or that it is available in Community Edition. Filed as a genuine documentation gap on this page rather than resolved here, since create-bucket.md never states the edition or bucket-type restriction itself.

cross_component_finding: This is the first PROCEDURAL page in the corpus to touch the bucket:couchbase-bucket/bucket:ephemeral-bucket closed two-member set, and it confirms round 17's reference-only finding directly from the UI: the Advanced Settings dialog is split into two named, mutually exclusive subsections keyed on Bucket Type (#couchbase-bucket-settings / #ephemeral-bucket-settings), and every one of Ejection Method, Ejection Policy, and available Minimum Durability Level values differs between them. It also SHARPENS round 17's durability finding: the exclusion is not limited to durability:level-persist-to-majority alone. The Couchbase-bucket Minimum Durability Level list has four members (none/majority/majorityAndPersistActive/persistToMajority); the Ephemeral-bucket list has only two (none/majority). Both excluded levels - not just the strongest one - require persistence to disk (majorityAndPersistActive persists to the ACTIVE node; persistToMajority persists to a MAJORITY of nodes), which is consistent with round 17's 'ephemeral buckets persist nothing' explanation but had not previously been evidenced for majorityAndPersistActive specifically.
